messages:
deploy-bot: Starting rollout for release/2026-03. Canary: model-serving stack -> 5% traffic in us-west-2. CI: http://ci/release/1234 :rocket:
Maria G.: getting a spike of 502s from inference-proxy-canary, started ~30s after canary traffic shifted
Kevin L.: I see increased 95th latency on model-serving-canary, traces look like connection resets to gpu-pool-3
Alex C.: can everyone check the canary dashboard? i'm not seeing canary-specific dashboards in the release view
srebot: Pager triggered: prod/model-serving.canary latency_slo.burn > 5% over 2m. Pager: oncall@pagerduty (severity=high) :rotating_light:
Sam P.: oncall here, joining. Maria — can you paste a sample request id or trace?
Maria G.: trace 0a1b2c... here's a snippet from the proxy logs:```2026-03-12T14:22:12Z ERR conn reset id=0a1b2c path=/v1/generate backend=gpu-pool-3```
Jules: I can't find canary tag in our dashboards either, looks like the release flag did not enable the canary metric tag in metrics-router config
Kevin L.: that explains missing graphs. alerts are firing at the service level but we don't have the canary split so it's noisy 
Alex C.: can we kill the feature flag for the new routing now? if we flip, traffic should fall back to stable routing immediately
Sam P.: agreed, i'm going to disable ff/rolling-route to stop canary. Command:```curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' https://flags.internal/api/ff/rolling-route/disable```
deploy-bot: Feature flag ff/rolling-route disabled by Sam P. at 2026-03-12T14:24:03Z :white_check_mark:
Maria G.: after kill — proxy errors dropping, 502s falling back down to baseline
Kevin L.: starting automated rollback of release/2026-03 from canary -> stable. Rolling traffic back to stable: 0 -> 0.0001 -> 0
srebot: Rollback job initiated by deploy-bot. Job ID: rb-2026-03-12-14-24
Alex C.: short note — observability gap: metrics-router didn't attach "canary=true" dimension when we enabled the new route. dashboards/alerts subset were keyed on that dimension so the canary looked invisible, and service-level alerts doubled up and looked noisy
Jules: that made SLO signal confusing — we saw a 5% burn but couldn't attribute to canary vs global quickly
Sam P.: quick customer-impact check: using traffic slice from edge logs, ~0.8% of total requests during the 3m window hit canary paths and experienced elevated error/latency. majority (~90%) recovered after flag kill. No major customer-facing incidents reported in support queue yet
Maria G.: re: support — ticketing: created internal ticket INF-2042 with sample traces and timeline, cc @support
Kevin L.: follow-up: alert dedupe rules kicked in poorly — both service-level and ingress-level alerts fired. Need to add a temporary silencing rule when rolling flags happen, or better: make canary metric dimension mandatory in metrics router
Sam P.: oncall handoff: i'm handing to Kevin for post-rollback monitoring. Kevin, i left commands and a checklist in thread: verify 5m, 10m, 30m windows; confirm steady-state token cost; confirm no residual rate-limits.
Kevin L.: taking handoff. Running quick checks now.
Alex C.: quick mitigation notes for postmortem: (1) metrics-router should default missing "canary" tag to "unknown" and dashboards must surface unknowns; (2) alert rules should prefer per-route SLOs where available, and fall back to service SLOs in a single consolidated alert rather than duplicate; (3) preflight for releases must validate dashboard presence for canary dimensions
Jules: adding action items to INF-2042 and assigning to eng-runtime + eng-sre
deploy-bot: Rollback completed for release/2026-03. All canary traffic removed at 2026-03-12T14:28:59Z
Maria G.: post-rollback: p95/p99 back to normal. no new errors in logs. marking incident resolved for now but opening follow-up for observability fixes
Sam P.: summary for pager duty: root cause = routing config omitted canary metric tag -> dashboards/alerts didn't show canary split -> noisy service alerts -> oncall invoked and we killed ff + rolled back. customer impact small (~0.8% requests affected), no escalations.
Kevin L.: will draft short incident note and link to postmortem doc later today. Suggested title: "missing canary metric tag during rollout caused noisy alerts and rollback"
Jules: tagging infra and devex for dashboard preflight automation. will fill timeline in INF-2042
Maria G.: thanks everyone. :heart:
Sam P.: closing handoff to Kevin. if anything spikes i'll re-open pager.
Kevin L.: ack, monitoring 30m then will post short postmortem link here
Jules: postmortem placeholder: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2042
deploy-bot: Incident thread closed (auto) at 2026-03-12T15:00:00Z
